Answer: C
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a curvilinear calcification outlining the heart, which is characteristic of constrictive pericarditis. The pacemaker lead seen in the images traverses the tricuspid valve and terminates in the right ventricle, consistent with standard placement. The definitive treatment for symptomatic constrictive pericarditis is surgical pericardiectomy (pericardial stripping).
